bullets.text: A dam safety emergency developed at Halvern Dam on the Sorrel River above Brindlemark in the Assek Valley from 9 September 2025, after the dam and its right abutment were reported damaged.

The alert level was raised from Yellow to Orange and a mandatory evacuation was ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow, later extending to Quennard as the evacuated figure rose from roughly 11,800 to 12,400.
No deaths, injuries or missing persons were reported in the window; the human impact was the displacement of Brindlemark and Quennard residents.
Brindlemark Police deployed to the town, assistance was provided in Quennard, and Sorrel Basin Water Authority and the dam operator issued information on the dam's condition.
Halvern Dam and its right abutment are reported damaged.
Sorrel Basin Water Authority and the operator issue information on the dam.
The alert level is raised from Yellow to Orange and a mandatory evacuation is ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow; roughly 11,800 residents leave the town.
The evacuated figure rises to 12,400 in Brindlemark and people are evacuated from Quennard; displaced residents move away from both towns.
Brindlemark Police deploy to Brindlemark and assistance is provided in Quennard.
Halvern Dam and its right abutment were damaged.
A mandatory evacuation was ordered for Brindlemark and Ferris Hollow when the alert level was raised to Orange.
Roughly 11,800 residents were evacuated from Brindlemark in the first phase of the mandatory evacuation.
The evacuated figure rose to 12,400 in Brindlemark, and people were also evacuated from Quennard.
Displaced residents moved away from Brindlemark and Quennard.
Brindlemark Police deployed to Brindlemark during the evacuation.
The alert level was raised from Yellow to Orange as the mandatory evacuation was ordered.
Sorrel Basin Water Authority and the dam operator issued information on the condition of Halvern Dam.
Assistance was provided to evacuees in Quennard.
